title: manually-fired PR gate posted its review but no relay reached the design thread

provenance.source: chatroom body + PR review timeline (operator lane note relayed as msg-2734)

not_representable_reason: Three-layer structural residual (Bohr msg-2831 §3(a), Einstein msg-2749 §5). (schema layer) no unit kind carries a GitHub review event's timestamp alongside the design thread reference the review was meant to relay into — the cross-artifact pair 'a review was posted' vs 'thread head' is unrepresentable in v1; (granularity layer) even with a per-review completion field a single design thread can await multiple reviews across multiple PRs, so the field would have to live on the review-relay request, not on the containing ThreadState (Einstein E-10); (consumer layer) scripts/parked_humans.py reads only the thread head's NEXT: line, so 'a review landed but was not relayed' cannot be distinguished from 'no review has landed yet' by the consumer that shapes the human-parked digest (Einstein E-9). Absent all three, the incident and its valid-wait counterexample construct byte-equivalent ThreadState objects — see test_m6_collision_pin_incident_equivalent_to_valid_wait for the machine assertion.

notes: Observed 2026-09-08 (Bohr msg-2744 §5 M-6): a manually-fired PR-gate review was posted on a mindwire PR but its design thread received no relay msg, so the thread head continued to name a role that had already acted. This class of stall — 'the awaited actor acted on a different surface, but nothing on the thread reflects it' — is the same family as M-5 in cause but a different surface pairing (GitHub review vs. Tier-C merge). Recorded here so the corpus preserves the incident without poisoning it as a spurious 'stall' verdict indistinguishable from a legitimate pre-review wait.
